🧠 Crypto News Brief: Risk-on is back: nearly $1B poured into spot Bitcoin ETFs as BTC briefly topped $87K, while Europe's central bank and the SEC pushed tokenization forward. Washington's post-Clarity fight is now shifting to the midterms. 💰 Spot Bitcoin ETFs Pull In Nearly $1B, Biggest Day in 11 Months U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in roughly $999 million on Monday, their strongest day since October 2025, led by BlackRock's IBIT, ARK/21Shares' ARKB and Fidelity's FBTC. Spot Ether ETFs added about $270 million. BTC briefly touched ~$87,300, its highest level since January, as $844 million in short positions were liquidated amid lower oil prices, easing yields and optimism ahead of this week's Trump–Xi meeting. Read full story 🏦 ECB to Invest Its Own Funds in Tokenized Securities The European Central Bank has begun preparatory work to invest a small part of its own-funds portfolio in tokenized, euro-denominated public-sector debt. Purchases will settle in central bank money through Pontes, the Eurosystem's newly launched DLT settlement service, with amounts and timing to be set by the Executive Board. More details 📜 SEC Sees First Tokenized-Stock Venues Launching Next Quarter SEC Crypto Task Force officials expect the first platforms operating under the new five-year Innovation Exemption to file notices as early as next quarter. The September 17 relief lets eligible venues offer permissioned trading of tokenized U.S.-listed stocks through AMM liquidity pools on public blockchains. Read more 🗳️ Crypto PAC Fairshake Commits $30M Against Sherrod Brown Crypto super PAC Fairshake will spend $30 million opposing former Senate Banking Committee chair Sherrod Brown in Ohio's Senate race, its most aggressive midterm move yet. The commitment comes days after the Clarity Act failed a Senate procedural vote, and the PAC says more midterm spending decisions are on the way. See details 🛡️ White Hats Move 52 BTC From Coldcard Exploit Into Recovery Trust Ethical hackers moved 52.37 BTC rescued from wallets exposed by July's Coldcard firmware flaw to an address controlled by the Wyoming-based Crypto Recovery Trust, Galaxy Digital research head Alex Thorn said. White hats have now swept about 40% of the bitcoin tied to the exploit's second wave to protect victims' funds.
